rationale: Start with a broad, moderately fast gradient to observe all 10 compounds while limiting late-elution penalties. The retention window and weakest resolutions will guide subsequent gradient and temperature adjustments.
Raise temperature while holding the gradient fixed to probe selectivity in the crowded middle cluster. The first run has ample time margin, so improving the critical pair is the priority.

Test the upper temperature limit to see whether the middle-cluster separation improves further or a new critical pair emerges. Keeping the gradient unchanged isolates the temperature effect and preserves the short elution window.

Use a shallower gradient at the best temperature tested to improve the remaining critical separation. The current last peak at 6.49 minutes provides room to increase resolution while aiming to keep all peaks within 10 minutes.

Combine an intermediate temperature with a moderately shallower gradient to balance the two temperature-sensitive separations. This should retain time margin below 10 minutes while testing whether both critical pairs can reach full resolution.

The maximum CRF is established; now shorten the gradient by one step to seek a faster fully resolved method. Keep temperature and endpoints fixed to assess whether both critical pairs remain at R ≥ 1.5.

Lower the starting organic fraction to test whether added early retention restores the critical separation with the shorter gradient. Injection 5 remains the fully resolved benchmark if this adjustment does not preserve both critical pairs.
Shorten the fastest fully resolved method by one gradient step to test its speed limit. Injection 7 remains the benchmark if either closely spaced pair falls below R = 1.5.

Probe a cooler selectivity regime for a potentially faster fully resolved method, since shortening at 55 C has reached a resolution limit. The broad gradient should still elute all compounds comfortably within the acquisition window.

Test a higher starting organic fraction at 50 C to shift middle-cluster selectivity and shorten retention. This explores a different route to full resolution while retaining injection 7 as the fastest proven fully resolved method.

Test a steeper gradient at 60 C to seek a faster selectivity regime beyond the middle-pair crossover. This may separate the pair that nearly coeluted at 60 C with the 10-minute gradient, while injection 7 remains the fully resolved fallback.

Raise the starting organic fraction one step from injection 5 to shorten the elution window while retaining its successful temperature and gradient duration. This tests whether the middle critical pairs remain resolved without compressing the first pair excessively.

Test a higher starting organic fraction with an intermediate slope in the high-temperature regime. This targets separation on the opposite side of the middle-pair crossover while seeking a substantially shorter elution window.

Test whether a shallower gradient resolves the middle cluster in the alternate elution order observed at 40 C. Comparing with injections 1 and 4 will help distinguish slope effects from temperature-driven selectivity changes.

Combine a higher starting organic fraction with a moderately shallow gradient in the promising 40 C regime. This tests whether the middle cluster can stay resolved while bringing the last peak substantially earlier than injection 14.

Refine around the fastest fully resolved method by slightly reducing the gradient slope. This tests whether the narrow resolution margins can be improved while keeping the last peak comfortably below 10 minutes.

Test whether a modest temperature decrease improves the alternate middle-cluster separation enough to permit a shorter gradient than at 40 C. The maximum-score methods remain secured, with injection 7 the fastest fully resolved result.

Reduce the endpoint by one step from injection 6 to interpolate between its insufficient resolution and injection 5’s fully resolved gradient slope. This targets the shortest fully resolved gradient at a starting organic fraction of 0.10.

Preserve injection 7’s successful gradient slope but end the ramp earlier, just beyond its observed elution window. This should retain full resolution and the approximately 7.6-minute last peak while shortening the programmed gradient.

Use a slope just shallower than injection 18 to lift its R = 1.47 pair above the full-credit threshold while preserving the other critical separation. This targets a fully resolved alternative near the fastest proven elution time, with slightly more balanced resolution margins.

Test a gradient slope between the fastest fully resolved method and injection 8’s faster but under-resolved method. This checks whether a modest reduction in last-peak time is possible while preserving R ≥ 1.5 for both critical pairs.

Back off one endpoint step from injection 18 to restore full resolution and test for a more balanced safety margin between the two critical pairs. The expected elution window remains comfortably below 10 minutes; injection 7 remains the fastest fully resolved benchmark.

Reduce the slope from injection 12 to restore its under-resolved middle pair while retaining the stronger separation of the other critical pair. This seeks a maximum-score method with larger resolution margins, while keeping the last peak below 10 minutes.

Lower the endpoint one more step from injection 23 to bring its R = 1.41 pair above 1.5 while preserving the other critical separation. This should provide a fully resolved alternative with stronger resolution margins and a last peak still below 10 minutes.

With the maximum CRF already secured, use the final injection to test whether a slightly shallower gradient gives both critical pairs a larger resolution margin while keeping the last peak below 10 minutes. Injections 7 and 19 remain the fastest proven fully resolved methods.
